audit.whatIsWrong: The page has Aurora's W and E swapped throughout. It calls E a 'point-and-click blink' and W a 'spirit zone / exile'. Riot: W is Across the Veil — a leap that turns her invisible on landing, 22s at rank 1; E is The Weirding — a blast that damages and slows, after which she hops backward, 15s. The page also names Twofold Hex (Q, 9s poke missile with a recast) as 'her escape'.
audit.why: Every trade instruction on the page is keyed to the wrong ability and the wrong cooldown. A player baiting 'her E blink' is baiting a 15s slow while the real 22s escape stays up.
audit.corrected: focus/dosFull[0]/report[5].t/breakdown.cooldowns and the content prose now name Across the Veil as the escape with its 22s rank-1 cooldown, The Weirding as the slow-and-hop, and Between Worlds as a slow zone she can teleport across.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Maokai levels 2, 3, first item and 2+ items while every why and spike on the same page says Aurora owns 2 through 6 and the late game, and Maokai's only favoured stage is first item.
audit.why: 48.19% over 83 games, the packet chart and the prose all agree with each other and disagree with the chart. The mirror audit independently found levels 2 and 3 should read Aurora.
audit.corrected: Rows 1,2,3,4,6 flipped to Aurora in both layers with ratings dropped to match; row 5 stays Maokai (his one window), row 0 stays Skill.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] is the first-item window but its 'when' field said 'Lvl 6', and the level-6 spike gave no reason beyond 'she just blinks it'.
audit.why: The stage label contradicted the text a reader is looking at. Between Worlds is 140s at rank 1 and creates a slow field she can teleport across — that, not a blink, is why Nature's Grasp fails to catch her.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].when set to '1st item'; whys[4] and mid rebuilt on Between Worlds' real behaviour.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sap Magic's real rule was absent: its cooldown drops each time Maokai casts a spell or is struck by an enemy spell.
audit.why: Her Twofold Hex poke therefore charges his heal — poke does not grind him down the way the page implies.

edits.before: Level 1 is the one stage you aren't behind — you have a single ability and she only has her Q poke, so nothing decisive happens. The trouble starts at 2-3: your whole trade is W-dash root into Q-knockback, and her E is a hard, point-and-click blink that flickers her straight out of your W. Every time you commit she's already gone and chipping you with Q from range. Don't throw W on cooldown hoping it lands — bait the E first with a fake step-up, drop E saplings on her poke spots, and accept you're farming down a bit rather than winning the early war.
edits.after: Level 1 is the one stage you aren't behind — you have a single ability and she only has Twofold Hex, so nothing decisive happens. The trouble starts at 2-3: your whole trade is W-dash root into Q-knockback, and Across the Veil leaps her clear and turns her invisible on landing. Every time you commit she's already gone and chipping you from range. Don't throw W on cooldown hoping it lands — bait the leap with a fake step-up, sapling her poke spots, and accept you're farming down a bit rather than winning the early war.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 she keeps the edge because her Q poke and W spirit zone out-range everything you have, and her E means your root never lands clean on cooldown. Your sustain is the equalizer, not your damage — proc Sap Magic on her whenever you do connect and heal the poke back. Level 6 doesn't swing the 1v1 much; R is a long-range engage that telegraphs, and she just blinks the bramble wave. Your real opening is First Item: as a Bami/sustain wall she physically can't burst you, so that's the stage to force the all-in on her E timer.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 she keeps the edge because Twofold Hex out-ranges everything you have and The Weirding slows you before hopping her clear, so your root rarely lands. Sustain is the equalizer, not damage — and every spell she hits you with shortens Sap Magic, so trade back the moment you connect. Level 6 doesn't swing the 1v1: Between Worlds slows inside its field and lets her teleport across it. Your real opening is First Item — as a Bami wall she can't burst you, so force the all-in on her 22s leap.
